observations.statement: The core defines seven UI-command mappings: graph HITL denial, health provider-setup opening, and five LSP actions (code action, find references, format document, format selection, and go to definition).
cmd.graph.deny_hitl declares no expected event, classifies its effect as a receipt, names cmd.graph.deny_hitl.dispatch_receipt, and requires either a no-persist receipt or route/open disposition.
cmd.health.provider_setup.open is routed to handlers::health::provider_setup_open and must emit health.route_opened with dispatch-correlation evidence.
Each of the five LSP mappings states that no persisted event is declared, requires a receipt or route/open disposition, and tests for the absence of unexpected persisted domain events.
All seven commands must be registered with typed arguments and a result contract.
Every mapping names a projected availability selector and a disabled-reason projection.
The graph-deny dispatch evidence must preserve command_id, origin, correlation_id, handler target, result, and receipt or event effect.

The graph-deny control explicitly requires stable role/name/description semantics, keyboard reachability and activation when visible, deterministic visible-focus behavior after dispatch or error, and assistive-technology exposure of its disabled reason.
Production certification for graph denial requires render/control, dispatcher, typed payload/result, projected-state, disabled-reason, receipt/event, accessibility, and regression evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Graph denial can certify without proving a denial occurred
candidate_findings.statement: For cmd.graph.deny_hitl, the core declares no expected event and accepts a receipt or route/open disposition; it contains no command-specific oracle that identifies the affected HITL request or proves that the request entered a denied state.
candidate_findings.impact: A handler that records only a dispatch artifact could satisfy the stated effect test while failing to perform the named domain operation.

candidate_findings.title: The five LSP actions lack operation-result oracles
candidate_findings.statement: Code action, find references, format document, format selection, and go to definition are each certified at the effect layer by a receipt or disposition and the absence of unexpected events; the core does not define the returned actions, references, edits, or destination that would prove the named operation succeeded.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can reach the named handlers and produce receipts while returning incorrect or empty operation results without violating the stated effect assertions.

candidate_findings.title: Typed payload and result obligations have no concrete schemas
candidate_findings.statement: All seven entries require typed arguments and a result contract, but the core supplies no fields, domain or primitive types, requiredness, defaults, validation and rejection rules, or result variants for any command.
candidate_findings.impact: UI, dispatcher, handlers, fixtures, and tests can implement mutually incompatible contracts while each claiming to satisfy the generic typed-contract requirement.

candidate_findings.title: health.route_opened is not an exact route-event contract
candidate_findings.statement: The health command names health.route_opened and correlation metadata, but the core does not specify the route identifier or destination, event payload and validation, emission cardinality or timing, ordering, or whether emission is transactional with a successful result.
candidate_findings.impact: Different implementations can emit the same event type for different destinations or at different lifecycle points and still satisfy the declared event test.

candidate_findings.title: Authority for denying HITL is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The graph-deny entry names a command, handler, and availability path but does not identify the actor, owning authority, permission or policy precondition, or the required rejection behavior for an unauthorized denial attempt.
candidate_findings.impact: Authorization can be implemented inconsistently or omitted, and the stated acceptance evidence has no oracle for access-control enforcement.

candidate_findings.title: Availability and disabled-reason state is path-only
candidate_findings.statement: The core names availability and disabled-reason paths for each command but does not define their value domains, nullability, consistency invariant, transition triggers, freshness, loading or stale states, or how a projected change controls dispatch eligibility.
candidate_findings.impact: Controls can disagree about when they are enabled and what disabled reason is exposed, especially while projected state changes.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt versus route/open disposition is not adjudicated
candidate_findings.statement: cmd.graph.deny_hitl is classified as effect_kind receipt and names a dispatch_receipt reference, yet its description permits either a no-persist receipt or a route/open disposition without stating when the alternative applies or whether the artifacts are equivalent.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders and certification tests can choose different accepted effect artifacts, making dispatch evidence and downstream consumption non-deterministic.

candidate_findings.title: Dispatch-correlation evidence lacks envelope semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The graph and health entries enumerate command_id, origin, correlation_id, handler target, result, and receipt or event effect, but do not define field types, requiredness, correlation-id creation and uniqueness, persistence, ordering, or representation on failure.
candidate_findings.impact: Evidence producers and consumers can serialize or correlate the same dispatch incompatibly, weakening traceability and reproducible acceptance.

candidate_findings.title: Lifecycle, retry, cancellation, and failure behavior is absent
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires dispatch results and effect evidence, and mentions focus after error, but does not define timeout, cancellation, retryability, idempotency, duplicate suppression, concurrent-dispatch ordering, partial failure, rollback, or error-result taxonomy.
candidate_findings.impact: Repeated, concurrent, cancelled, or failed commands can produce divergent domain and GUI behavior while remaining consistent with the stated wiring checks.

candidate_findings.title: Graph-deny accessibility acceptance is not exact
candidate_findings.statement: The graph-deny contract requires a stable role/name/description, keyboard activation when visible, deterministic focus return, and a disabled announcement, but does not prescribe the role, accessible name or description, visibility predicate, activation keys, focus destination and timing, or announcement text.
candidate_findings.impact: Materially different accessibility behaviors can all satisfy the categorical regression requirement, and deterministic automated assertions cannot be derived from this window alone.

candidate_findings.title: Production-certification evidence has no artifact or adjudication contract
candidate_findings.statement: The graph-deny entry enumerates required evidence categories but does not define artifact schemas, pass/fail thresholds, evidence issuer or authority, retention, version binding, or how conflicting evidence is resolved.
candidate_findings.impact: Certification can be assembled and judged differently by separate builders or reviewers even when they use the same evidence-category list.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Each of the seven commands has an exact dispatcher-to-handler reachability requirement.
Availability and disabled-reason projection paths are explicitly named for every command.
The six commands with no declared persisted event explicitly require a receipt or disposition and assert that no unexpected persisted domain event is emitted.
The health command declares the exact expected event type health.route_opened and requires command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target in its event test.
The graph-deny entry explicitly covers role/name/description semantics, keyboard access, focus behavior after dispatch or error, disabled-state announcement, and an accessibility regression check.

The graph-deny production-certification requirement explicitly enumerates render/control, dispatcher, typed-contract, projected-state, disabled-reason, receipt/event, accessibility, and regression evidence.
Graph-deny and health-provider dispatch evidence explicitly preserves correlation and handler-target fields rather than relying only on handler reachability.

unknowns.statement: The exact argument fields, types, validation, and result variants for all seven commands are unknown within this window.
The target HITL request, denial reason, required state change, and dispatch-receipt content for cmd.graph.deny_hitl are unknown.
The actor and permission authority allowed to invoke cmd.graph.deny_hitl are unknown.
Availability and disabled-reason types, transition rules, update triggers, and stale or loading behavior are unknown.
The selection rule, schema, persistence, retention, authority, and consumer for a receipt versus a route/open disposition are unknown.
The route destination, event payload, emission count, timing, ordering, and transactional boundary of health.route_opened are unknown.
The document or selection context, document-version handling, operation-specific outputs, and application semantics for the five LSP commands are unknown.
Ordering, cancellation, timeout, retry, idempotency, duplicate, and concurrency behavior for dispatch are unknown.
The error taxonomy, error result, user-visible error projection, retry affordance, and failure-evidence representation are unknown.
The exact accessible role, name, description, visibility predicate, keyboard keys, focus return destination and timing, and disabled-announcement copy are unknown.
The artifact format, pass threshold, certifying authority, retention, and version binding of production-certification evidence are unknown.
Downstream consumers and owners of cmd.graph.deny_hitl.dispatch_receipt and health.route_opened are not named in the core.
